Bagpat, Up. ............Driver/Respondent no. 1 2. Alok Kumar S/o Sh. Ashok Kumar, R/o D-42, Gf West Jyoti Nagar Ext. Sabapur, Shahdara, Delhi. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 3. National Ins. Co. texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178596883/ 1 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 06.11.2020 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the facts of the case, on 12.06.2018 at about 11.30 PM, when the injured / claimant was going on his scooty bearig no. DL 12SH 5495 towards Sangam Vihar via M. B. road and reached in front of Majidia Hospital main gate, R.D Marg New Delhi, the alleged offending vehicle bearig no. HR 55A 7158, being driven by, as per the claim of claimant, by R-1 in rash and negligent manner and at a very high speed, hit the victim from back side and due to sudden and forceful impact, he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injury all over his body. 3. Victim was taken to AIIMS Trauma Center and medically examined ad MLC was prepared. He remained admitted for 21 days and thereafter also his medical treatment continued and thereafter he was bed rest for 6 months. 4. Accordingly the charge sheet u/s 279, 338 IPC filed against the R-1. Further, present DAR also filed. MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 2 of 22 5. Further, as per record, R-1 & 2 participated in proceedings in the beginning but they did not file their reply and their right to file reply stands closed by my Ld. Predecessor. 6. Further, reply/ report filed by insurance company dated 02.11.2018 in which no legal offer was given and case was contested. It is stated on behalf of insurance company that there is no site plan of alleged incident and there is no statement of the petitioner or injured or any eye witness to the alleged accident and FIR was registered at the instance of police official. As such, it is alleged that IO was acting in connivance with claimant to raise the present unjustified claim. It is further stated that name of injured was not mentioned in the MLC. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Predecessor of this Tribunal on 05.11.2018: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 12.06.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR 55K 7158 (Truck) being driven by R1 & owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP. 2. Relief. 8. As per record, injured Jitender examined himself as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary Jitender vs . Sabir Ali & Ors. on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178596883/ 2 and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/6 (colly) relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. 8. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 3 of 22 insurance company/R-3. Further, such cross examination was adopted on behalf of R-1 & 2. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 10. Further, as per record, None of the respondent led any evidence. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178596883/ 3 16. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1, it is noted that PW-1/Victim/Injured deposed on the lines of claimant's original stand, which is already noted above. It was further deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of the R-1, the accident in question took place. 17. During cross examination by Ld. Counsel for insurance company, PW-1/ injured deposed that he saw the offending vehicle which was a truck before he became unconscious.
texts.arguments: Including in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 14. Further, in the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 4 of 22 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. Including in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble High Court that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 15. It may further be noted that including in the case of Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it is held by Hon'ble Supreme Court/ Hon'ble High Court that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 6 of 22 person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 22. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) Jitender vs . Sabir Ali & Ors. on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178596883/ 4 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. 22.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 22.7. 28. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that income loss for 6 months is not proved on record and it is claimed that actual loss of income, if any is of much lesser period. 29. Minimum wages for a skilled worker at the time of accident on 12.06.2018 in Delhi was Rs. 16,858/- which is more than the income claimed by the claimant. Accordingly, it is presumed and held that petitioner was earning at least Rs. 16,858/- per month at the time of accident. 30. Further, having regard to the nature of injury and medical treatment period and nature of treatment, it is held that there is a loss of income of 4 months. It is further argued by petitioner side that accordingly functional disability of at least of 28% in relation to whole body be taken in the present case, as he was doing skill job of electrician and suffered injuries in left lower limb. 32. On the other hand, it is argued by Ld. Counsel or insurance company that there is no functional disability of 28 % in any case, in the present case. It is further argued that there is no functional disability at all. It is further submitted that only MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 11 of 22 vague nature of job as electrician is mentioned without any material in this regard. 33. Regarding compensation towards future prospect having regard to the ratio of judgment of Rajkumar (Supra) read with facts of present case, it is noted that petitioner claimed that he was doing electrician work but no details thereof is given but at the same time, even if he was doing any work of skill wages level, the same require active walking, standing and working and physical strength is predominant factor in such type of minimum wages jobs. 34. 40. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and the MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 16 of 22 demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Jitender vs . Sabir Ali & Ors. 42. Keeping in view the entirety of the facts and circumstances involved in the present case and the abovesaid guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and Hon'ble Supreme Court, as petitioner is in growing years, out of compensation amount/Award amount: Jitender vs . Sabir Ali & Ors. on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178596883/ 11 43. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, MACT No.: 927/18 Jitender Vs. Sabir Ali & Ors. Page No. 19 of 22 Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s). However, the statement containing FDR number, FDR amount, date of maturity and maturity amount shall be furnished by bank to the claimant(s). (c) The monthly interest be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the claimant(s) near the place of their residence. (d) The maturity amounts of the FDR(s) be credited by Electronic Clearing System (ECS) in the savings bank account of the claimant (s) near the place of their residence. (e) No loan, advance, withdrawal or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the fixed deposits without permission of the Court. (f) The concerned bank shall not be issue any cheque book and/or debit card to claimant(s).
